headline: Union Minister for Law & Justice (I/C) Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal launches revamped India Code Portal at the Legislative Department
fullText:
Ministry of Law and Justice

Union Minister for Law & Justice (I/C) Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal launches revamped India Code Portal at the Legislative Department

Revamped portal to make access to laws simpler, faster and more citizen-centric

AI-assisted search, semantic and speech search, improved navigation and multilingual access among key features

13 AUG 2026 8:54PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, today, on 13th August, 2026, launched the revamped India Code Portal at Kartavya Bhavan 2, New Delhi, in the august presence of Shri R. Venkataramani, Attorney General for India, Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs, Dr. Manoj Kumar, Additional Secretary, and senior officers of the Legislative Department. Shri Priyank Bharti, Director General, National Informatics Centre (NIC), Shri Sudeep Shrivastava, Chief Operating Officer, IndiaAI Mission and senior officers of the NIC were also present on the occasion.

The revamped portal marks an important step in the Government’s continuing endeavour to make access to laws simpler, faster, wider and more citizen-centric, using contemporary digital technologies.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal underscored the importance of the Constitution and of ensuring that laws are easily accessible, understandable and available to all stakeholders. He observed that the India Code Portal serves as a reliable and comprehensive platform for citizen-friendly access to the Constitution, Central Acts, Rules and other legislative information. Highlighting the role of technology in strengthening access to law, he appreciated the dedicated efforts of the officers and officials of the Legislative Department in conceptualising, coordinating and overseeing the revamp, as well as the NIC team for its technical expertise and development support. Shri Meghwal noted that this collaborative effort would significantly enhance the accessibility, transparency and citizen-centric delivery of legislative information.

Shri R. Venkataramani, Attorney General for India, highlighted the transformation from physical to digital access to laws and appreciated the revamped India Code Portal developed by the Legislative Department with several new and user-friendly features. He emphasized the importance of keeping the portal technologically updated and responsive to emerging requirements. He also stressed the responsibility of legislative officers to contribute towards clear, effective and quality legislation and underscored the importance of ensuring wider and convenient access to laws. He appreciated the coordinated efforts of the Legislative Department and the technical team in developing the revamped portal, which would further strengthen transparency and public access to legislative information.

Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs, outlined the evolution of the India Code Portal and the efforts to make authentic and updated legislative information easily accessible to citizens, legal professionals, government departments and other stakeholders. Highlighting the role of technology in improving dissemination and access to laws, he outlined the key features of the revamped portal, including its more user-friendly interface and enhanced search, navigation and accessibility. He appreciated the coordinated efforts of the Legislative Department and the National Informatics Centre (NIC) and expressed confidence that the revamped platform would significantly strengthen wider and easier public access to reliable legislative information.

Dr Manoj Kumar, Additional Secretary, Legislative Department, introduced the revamped India Code Portal and outlined its key features and the larger vision behind its transformation. He observed that access to law is the first step towards access to justice and that laws must not only be available, but also easy to find, navigate, understand and use. He highlighted that the revamped portal seeks to move India Code beyond being a repository of legislative documents towards becoming an accessible, interconnected and citizen-centric digital gateway to law, with improved search and navigation, linkages between Acts and subordinate legislation, integration with the e-Gazette ecosystem, AI-assisted and semantic search, speech-enabled access and multilingual capabilities. He emphasised that technology should reduce the distance between the law and the citizen and enable legislative information to become more discoverable, interoperable and usable, thereby strengthening transparency, legal awareness and citizen-centric governance.

India Code provides a unified digital repository of Central Acts and their subordinate legislations, State Acts and their subordinate legislations, as well as Union Territory legislations and regulations. The revamped portal significantly enhances the manner in which citizens, legal professionals, researchers, the judiciary and Government can search, navigate and access legislative information through improved and intelligent search capabilities, AI-assisted search and interaction, semantic and speech-based search, easier navigation across legislations, access to amendments and legislative history, linkage of Acts with relevant subordinate legislation, integration with the e-Gazette ecosystem, improved document viewing, QR-enabled access and a structured citizen-feedback mechanism. It also seeks to enable AI-assisted multilingual access to laws in all 22 languages included in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution, thereby making access to law wider, easier and more citizen-centric across Bharat.

The technological revamp seeks to transform India Code from being merely an online repository of legislation into a digital gateway to law, supported by an increasingly interconnected and citizen-friendly legal information architecture.

The initiative is aligned with the larger objective of leveraging technology for ease of accessing law, transparency, wider citizen participation and improved delivery of legal and public services.

The revamped India Code Portal represents an important step towards building a trusted and technology-enabled legal information ecosystem for Bharat, where laws are increasingly searchable, accessible, interconnected and available to citizens in the language and form most convenient to them.

headline: DRI busts illegal drug manufacturing facility in Jewar, UP; 30 kg drugs seized and two persons arrested
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

DRI busts illegal drug manufacturing facility in Jewar, UP; 30 kg drugs seized and two persons arrested

30 kg precursor chemicals to be used for manufacture of drugs, and complete equipment and apparatus also seized

13 AUG 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its sustained crackdown on the illicit manufacture and trafficking of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has busted another clandestine drug manufacturing facility. The facility was found operating from a residential premises in the Jewar area of Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh.

On 09/10 Aug 2026, an intelligence-led operation of DRI, resulted in the seizure of approximately 30 kg Amphetamine/intermediary forms, around 30 kg precursor chemicals, to be used for manufacture of drugs, and complete equipment and apparatus used for clandestine manufacture of psychotropic substances.

Various chemicals, equipment and contraband recovered from the premise.

Search of the premises revealed a fully equipped clandestine manufacturing set-up, comprising electrical furnaces, hose pipes, scientific and measuring equipment, reagents and other equipment and tools required for manufacture of psychotropic substances. Multiple liquid containers containing various precursor chemicals, raw materials and reagents were also recovered from the premises, along with white-coloured powdery/crystalline substances stored in different containers, whose testing with field kits indicated the presence of amphetamine, a psychotropic substance scheduled under Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act 1985.

The recoveries, along with the manufacturing apparatus, amphetamine and chemicals found at the premises, indicate the existence of a clandestine facility being used for illicit manufacture of psychotropic substances in contravention of the provisions of the (NDPS) Act, 1985. A foreign national and his Indian female associate, who were operating the clandestine facility, were arrested under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985.

Preliminary investigation indicated the accused persons would bring manufacturing equipment and raw materials to the premises during night hours, set up and operate the facility for about a week, and thereafter would remove the equipment and clean the premises. The same cycle was reportedly repeated after a gap of two to three months, apparently to avoid suspicion among local residents.

Recent DRI action against clandestine drug manufacturing

The present operation is result of DRI's intensified focus on dismantling clandestine drug manufacturing infrastructure and the networks supporting illicit production and trafficking. In the past one month, DRI has busted three other clandestine manufacturing facilities—a Mephedrone manufacturing facility at Ankleshwar, Gujarat, where Mephedrone and substantial quantities of precursor chemicals were seized and three persons arrested; an Alprazolam and Diazepam manufacturing facility in Satara, Maharashtra, where finished and intermediary psychotropic substances and approximately 400 litres of raw materials were seized and two persons arrested; and a Tramadol manufacturing and export network centred in Ambernath, Maharashtra, linked to an attempted export of 1 lakh Tramadol to Nigeria, resulting in the arrest of three key accused persons.

These successive operations demonstrate DRI's continued focus on identifying and dismantling the entire ecosystem of illicit drug manufacture—from procurement of precursor chemicals and establishment of clandestine laboratories to financing, trafficking, storage and attempted export of narcotics drugs and psychotropic substances. The operations also highlight the increasingly sophisticated methods adopted by drug trafficking networks to conceal manufacturing activities and evade detection.

headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Milestone achieved in global climate action
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Milestone achieved in global climate action

13 AUG 2026 8:11PM by PIB Delhi

India’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) comprises of three quantitative targets namely the reduction of overall emissions intensity of our Gross Domestic Product (GDP), enhancing share of non-fossil fuel-based energy resources in installed electric power capacity and creation of additional carbon sink.

India had achieved a reduction of 37.38% in the emissions intensity of its GDP in 2022 from the 2005 level, against the NDC goal of reducing emissions intensity by 45% by 2030. The share of cumulative installed electric power capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy sources crossed 50% in June 2025, thereby achieving the NDC goal five years ahead of the committed timeline. As of 30th June 2026, non-fossil fuel-based energy resources accounted for 54.18% of the country’s total installed electric power capacity. India has created an additional carbon sink of 2.44 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent during 2005 to 2022, against the NDC goal of creating an additional carbon sink of 2.5–3.0 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent by 2030 through additional forest and tree cover.

As reported in India’s first Biennial Transparency Report submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in April, 2026, the decoupling of greenhouse gas emissions from economic growth and GDP can be attributed to policies promoting renewable energy deployment, improving the energy efficiency of all economic activity. The early achievement of NDC goal on share of non-fossil fuel based installed electric power capacity has been made possible by a range of policies that incentivize renewable energy generation and its integration in to national electricity grid. The creation of carbon sink could be possible because of high priority accorded to conservation and restoration by the national and the State governments. The approach is reflected in the framework of Policies, Acts, Rules, Programmes and Schemes to ensure conservation of forests and biodiversity, enhance green cover and participation of people in the conservation activities while protecting rights of forest dependent communities.

The NDC targets for the year 2035 have been enhanced, with quantitative targets to reduce the emissions intensity of GDP by 47% from the 2005 level, achieve 60% cumulative installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy resources, and create carbon sink of 3.5 to 4.0 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent through forest and tree cover as compared to the baseline year of

2005. The NDC also includes five qualitative targets aimed at promoting sustainable lifestyles, enhancing adaptation capacity and adoption of climate friendly cleaner path aligned with the goal of Viksit Bharat @2047.

India's progress in implementing its significant climate commitments has received wide recognition from many leading international bodies including the International Energy Agency (IEA), Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), United Nationals Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), World Bank, International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), etc.

This information was provided by MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE, SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH, in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today.

(Rajya Sabha US Q2928)

(Release ID: 2299186)

India has achieved key Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) targets ahead of schedule, including a 37.38% reduction in emissions intensity of GDP by 2022, surpassing 50% non-fossil fuel-based installed electric power capacity in June 2025, and creating an additional carbon sink of 2.44 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change provided this update in response to a parliamentary question on 13 August 2026.  

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS  
- **Emissions Intensity**: Achieved a 37.38% reduction in emissions intensity of GDP in 2022 compared to 2005 levels, against the NDC target of 45% by 2030.

headline: Government Strengthens Welfare, Healthcare and Social Security Measures for Senior Citizens
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Government Strengthens Welfare, Healthcare and Social Security Measures for Senior Citizens

AVYAY, Healthcare and Social Security Measures Strengthen Support for India’s Growing Elderly Population

13 AUG 2026 8:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has taken a comprehensive range of measures to address the growing needs of senior citizens and ensure their welfare, healthcare, social security and dignified living.

According to written information provided by the Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B.L. Verma in the Lok Sabha to Shri Yadhuveer Wadiyar, India’s elderly population is projected to increase from 10 crore in 2011 to 23 crore by 2036, with its share in the total population rising from 8.4 per cent to 14.9 per cent.

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) as an umbrella scheme for the welfare of senior citizens across the country. The scheme comprises seven components covering areas such as shelter and care, State-level interventions, grievance redressal, assistive devices, innovative solutions, geriatric caregiving and other initiatives for healthy and productive ageing.

During the last three years, from 2023-24 to 2025-26, a total of 10,00,456 beneficiaries were covered under AVYAY, 2,21,30,687 beneficiaries under NSAP and 28,29,63,879 beneficiaries under NPHCE.

Under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC), grants-in-aid are provided to Non-Governmental and Voluntary Organisations for running and maintaining Senior Citizens Homes and Continuous Care Homes, where indigent senior citizens are provided facilities including shelter, nutrition, Medicare and entertainment free of cost. The State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC) supports States and Union Territories for activities including awareness generation, sensitisation, cataract surgeries and other State-specific initiatives.

The Government has also strengthened grievance redressal and support services through Elderline, the National Helpline for Senior Citizens. The toll-free helpline 14567, launched on October 1, 2021, provides grievance redressal services and generates awareness among senior citizens regarding relevant Acts, schemes and programmes of the Central and State Governments.

Under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY), senior citizens with a monthly income of not more than ₹15,000 and suffering from age-related disabilities or infirmities are provided physical aids and assisted-living devices aimed at restoring near-normal bodily functions. The scheme, launched on April 1, 2017, is implemented through Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO), a Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

The Seniorcare Ageing Growth Engine (SAGE) component promotes innovative solutions for problems commonly faced by the elderly. Innovative start-ups are identified and encouraged to develop products, processes and services for the welfare of senior citizens, with Government investment in the equity of selected firms not exceeding 49 per cent of their total equity.

To address the increasing demand for professional elderly care, the Government is also implementing the Training of Geriatric Care Givers component, aimed at bridging the gap between the supply and demand for trained geriatric caregivers and creating a professional cadre in the field of geriatric care.

Healthcare support for senior citizens is being strengthened through initiatives of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Under Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), health insurance coverage of ₹5 lakh is provided to all senior citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of their socio-economic status.

The National Programme for Healthcare of the Elderly (NPHCE) focuses on the health and well-being of senior citizens through a community-based primary healthcare approach, dedicated services at Primary and Community Health Centre levels, dedicated facilities at district hospitals, strengthening of Regional Geriatric Centres and information and education initiatives. The programme also provides for continuous monitoring, independent evaluation and research in geriatrics. The tertiary component of the Rashtriya Varishth Jan Swasthya Yojana has resulted in the establishment of 17 Regional Geriatric Centres and two National Centres of Ageing.

Social security support is also provided through the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development. Under the programme, eligible senior citizens receive a central pension share of ₹200 per month for those aged 60–79 years and ₹500 per month for those aged 80 years and above, with States and Union Territories providing additional top-ups.

The Government conducts periodic assessments of AVYAY to review its implementation and outcomes. Discussions are held with stakeholders to assess emerging needs and challenges faced by senior citizens, while third-party evaluations are undertaken before continuation of the scheme during a new financial cycle. The findings and recommendations of these evaluations are used to review implementation and identify emerging needs, with appropriate steps taken to mitigate hardships faced by senior citizens.

The Government’s multi-dimensional approach combines social care, healthcare, pension support, grievance redressal, assistive devices, geriatric caregiving and innovation to respond to the evolving needs of the country’s senior citizen population and promote a life of dignity, security and well-being for the elderly.

headline: Transforming Education through Smart Classrooms in SC-Dominated Villages: A Digital Learning Initiative in Kathua, Jammu and Kashmir
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Transforming Education through Smart Classrooms in SC-Dominated Villages: A Digital Learning Initiative in Kathua, Jammu and Kashmir

13 AUG 2026 8:02PM by PIB Delhi

Under the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY), District Kathua has taken significant strides towards bridging the digital divide in rural and border areas by establishing Smart Classrooms in Government Schools located in SC-dominated villages.

During the year 2022-23, a total of 07 Smart Classrooms were established under the PM-AJAY component in different Government Schools of SC-dominated villages. Notably, these included Chack Chabba and Chack Nathal, villages located near the International Border, and Village Sandhi, situated in the remotest sub-division of Bani. Each Smart Classroom included installation of Interactive Touch Panels, procurement of student furniture, and execution of essential civil works such as child-friendly wall paintings and electrification.

Building upon this success, 04 additional Smart Classrooms were established during 2023-24 under the same component. Further, in 2025-26, 03 more Smart Classrooms were added, thereby expanding the outreach of digital education in the district.

The establishment of Smart Classrooms has significantly enhanced the overall learning experience of students in rural and far-flung areas. Access to modern teaching tools, audio-visual content, and interactive learning—once limited to expensive private schools—has now reached Government Schools in remote villages with limited exposure to the outside world. For many students, modern digital education, once a distant dream, has become a reality, leading to improved classroom engagement, conceptual clarity, and academic outcomes.

headline: NMBA reaches, sensitizes more than 30.52 crore people across the country, this includes more than 11.87 crore youth and 8.45 crore women
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

NMBA reaches, sensitizes more than 30.52 crore people across the country, this includes more than 11.87 crore youth and 8.45 crore women

Central Government Strengthens Drug Demand Reduction and Rehabilitation Services in Jammu & Kashmir

Over 1.20 Crore People Sensitized under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan in Jammu & Kashmir

13 AUG 2026 8:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has undertaken a range of measures to strengthen prevention, treatment and rehabilitation services for substance use in Jammu & Kashmir under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), according to the reply given by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment in Rajya Sabha.

As per the National Survey on Extent and Pattern of Substance Use in India conducted by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment through the National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), AIIMS in 2018, opioids had a prevalence of 4.91 per cent in Jammu & Kashmir, with an estimated 5.40 lakh users in the 10–75 age group. Alcohol had a prevalence of 3.50 per cent with an estimated 3.90 lakh users, followed by sedatives at 1.54 per cent with 1.70 lakh estimated users, cannabis at 1.31 per cent with 1.40 lakh users and inhalants at 1.22 per cent with 1.35 lakh users.

In a written reply to Shri. Sajjad Ahmad Kichloo in the Rajya Sabha, the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B.L. Verma stated that the Government is supporting a network of treatment and rehabilitation facilities in Jammu & Kashmir. These include 1 Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA), 3 Outreach and Drop In Centres (ODICs), 2 Community based Peer Led Intervention (CPLI) programmes, 6 District De-Addiction Centres (DDACs) and 21 Addiction Treatment Facilities (ATFs).

The number of persons treated for drug addiction in centres supported by the Department in Jammu & Kashmir increased from 5,382 in 2021-22 to 46,491 in 2025-26. The annual figures were 27,843 in 2022-23, 36,588 in 2023-24 and 40,546 in 2024-25.

Under NAPDDR, the Ministry provides financial assistance to State Governments and Union Territory Administrations for preventive education, awareness generation, capacity building and drug demand reduction programmes. Assistance is also provided to NGOs and voluntary organisations for running and maintaining IRCAs, CPLIs, ODICs and DDACs, while Government hospitals are supported for establishing Addiction Treatment Facilities.

Across the country, NAPDDR-supported activities include 344 IRCAs, 45 CPLI programmes, 76 ODICs, 155 ATFs and 145 DDACs. IRCAs provide in-patient treatment along with counselling, detoxification/de-addiction, after-care and reintegration into the social mainstream. CPLI programmes focus on children below 18 years, while ODICs provide screening, assessment, counselling and referral and linkage to treatment and rehabilitation services.

The Ministry also maintains the toll-free de-addiction helpline 14446, which provides primary counselling and immediate referral services to persons seeking help. More than 4.6 lakh calls have been received through the helpline so far, including more than 11,000 calls from Jammu & Kashmir.

The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), launched on August 15, 2020 in 272 identified vulnerable districts, has since August 2023 been extended to all districts of the country. The campaign focuses on spreading awareness about substance use, particularly among higher educational institutions, university campuses and schools. With the support of States, NMBA has so far reached and sensitized more than 30.52 crore people across the country, including more than 11.87 crore youth and 8.45 crore women. Over 28.61 Lakh activities have been conducted in educational institutions while more than 28.29 Lakh persons have been treated and rehabilitated across the country, as on this date.

In Jammu & Kashmir, the campaign has sensitized more than 1.20 crore people, including over 69.14 lakh youth and 51.20 lakh women, through extensive awareness and outreach activities. A total of 8,565 Nasha Mukt Mitrs have joined the campaign in the Union Territory.

(Release ID: 2299177)

The Central Government is implementing a comprehensive suite of drug demand reduction and rehabilitation initiatives in Jammu & Kashmir under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), aimed at strengthening prevention, treatment, and recovery services for substance use disorders.

headline: Central Government Reaffirms Measures to Protect Rights and Promote Inclusion of LGBTQAI+ Community
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Central Government Reaffirms Measures to Protect Rights and Promote Inclusion of LGBTQAI+ Community

Measures cover legal protection, ration cards, banking, healthcare and safety of LGBTQAI+ community

13 AUG 2026 7:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has reiterated its commitment to ensuring the protection of rights, welfare and social inclusion of the LGBTQAI+ community, including intersex persons, through a range of legal, administrative and welfare measures across different social spheres.

In a written reply to Smt Rajathi in the Rajya Sabha, the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B.L. Verma, outlined measures being undertaken by various Ministries and Departments to improve participation of the LGBTQAI+ community in areas including education, employment, identity documentation and other entitlements.

The Government's response highlighted a multi-Ministry approach towards strengthening protection, access to services and social inclusion of the LGBTQAI+ community, covering food security, financial services, healthcare, protection from discrimination, and safety and dignity.

The Ministry stated that the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, as amended in 2026, provides a comprehensive legal framework for the protection and welfare of transgender persons. The Act includes intersex persons born with congenital variations within the definition of transgender person. The Act and the Rules framed thereunder provide protection against discrimination and facilitate access to welfare measures and other entitlements.

The Department of Food and Public Distribution has issued an advisory to all States and Union Territories clarifying that, under existing provisions, partners in a queer relationship are to be treated as part of the same household for the purposes of ration cards. States and UTs have also been advised to take necessary measures to ensure that such partners do not face discrimination in the issuance of ration cards.

The Department of Financial Services has issued an advisory clarifying that there are no restrictions on persons of the queer community opening a joint bank account. The advisory also permits a person in a queer relationship to be nominated to receive the balance in the account in the event of the death of the account holder.

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has issued communications to stakeholders, including States and UTs, for ensuring the rights of the LGBTQAI+ community in relation to healthcare. The measures include awareness activities, prohibition of conversion therapy, availability of sex reassignment surgery, changes in curricula, tele-consultation facilities, sensitisation and training of staff at various levels, and provisions relating to claiming the body where no near relative, next of kin or family member is available.

The Directorate General of Health Services has also issued a communication to State Health Departments and other stakeholders regarding ensuring healthcare access and reducing discrimination towards the LGBTQAI+ community.

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has framed guidelines concerning medical intervention required for infants and children with disorders of sexual differentiation (intersex), with the objective of enabling them to lead a medically normal life without complications. The Ministry is also working on guidelines addressing issues relating to the mental health and well-being of the queer community.

The Ministry of Home Affairs has issued an advisory to all States and UTs concerning prison visitation rights of the queer community. Another advisory has been issued regarding law-and-order measures to ensure that members of the queer community do not face threats of violence, harassment or coercion.

headline: Union Minister of Textiles to inaugurate Handloom Haat: The Handloom Experience Centre at Janpath on 14 August
fullText:
Ministry of Textiles

Union Minister of Textiles to inaugurate Handloom Haat: The Handloom Experience Centre at Janpath on 14 August

13 AUG 2026 7:07PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Textiles Shri Giriraj Singh will inaugurate Handloom Haat: The Handloom Experience Centre at Janpath, New Delhi, on 14 August 2026, marking a significant step towards creating a distinctive public destination for experiencing, understanding and engaging with India’s rich handloom heritage. The re-envisioned Handloom Haat will bring together heritage, knowledge, contemporary design, enterprise and retail under one roof.

The Handloom Experience Centre has been envisioned as a showcase of India’s handloom ecosystem, where traditional knowledge is not only preserved and interpreted, but actively practised, experienced and taken forward. Visitors will be able to explore the materials, processes, techniques and stories behind handwoven textiles, encounter contemporary expressions of handloom and discover products from weavers and handloom brands.

From Heritage to Contemporary Design

The inaugural showcase will feature 24 award-winning weavers through an exhibition organised by the National Handloom Development Corporation (NHDC), alongside 30+ curated brands participating through Weave The Future 5.0.

The fifth edition of ‘Weave The Future’ showcased in the ground and first floor will bring together weavers, designers, brands, researchers and other stakeholders to advance sustainable, circular and craft-led approaches to textiles. Its showcase at Handloom Haat will feature contemporary products developed through handloom and regenerative materials, with a focus on indigenous fibres, material innovation and responsible textile practices. It will also feature installations exploring India’s indigenous fibre landscape and the relationship between geography, agriculture, ecology and textile production.

The retail experience at Handloom Haat will therefore extend beyond conventional shopping, offering visitors an opportunity to discover the diversity, quality and contemporary relevance of Indian handlooms while creating greater visibility and market access for weavers and handloom enterprises.

A Multi-Layered Handloom Experience

The inauguration will offer guests a curated journey across the three floors of Handloom Haat, highlighting different dimensions of India’s handloom ecosystem.

As part of the inaugural experience, a temporary exhibition, on the ground floor, titled “Reimagining Odisha Weaves — Cloth | Craft | Creativity | Community” by Vriksh Designs will showcase how contemporary design can revitalise regional textile traditions through collaboration between designers and master weavers. The exhibition will highlight the revival of lesser-known and forgotten Odisha traditions such as Ganjam Bomkai and Dhalapathar Tapestry, alongside innovations in Ikat, Jaala and Phoda weaving, natural dyes, new colourways, textures, motifs and product forms.

The first floor will centre on the Visvakarma Gallery, a permanent gallery, bringing together rare textiles from the landmark Visvakarma exhibition series (1981–1991), which brought together weavers, designers, scholars and cultural patrons in an exploration of India’s diverse handloom traditions. Produced through Weavers’ Service Centres in close collaboration with weaving communities, these textiles demonstrate the coming together of technical skill, creative imagination and contemporary inquiry in Post-independent India. This gallery will also pay a tribute to Sant Kabir awardees and Padma Shri awardees, recognising individual practitioners whose exceptional contributions have expanded the practice, understanding and visibility of Indian handlooms.

The second floor will feature Design Conclave and an immersive experience that will take visitors on a visual and sensory journey inspired by India’s forests and the rich repertoire of animal, bird, floral and natural motifs found across diverse handloom traditions.

A New Destination for Handloom Excellence, Experience and Enterprise

The re-envisioned Handloom Haat aims to strengthen the visibility and market presence of Indian handlooms while creating opportunities for weavers, designers and handloom enterprises. By bringing together heritage, contemporary practice, retail and public engagement, it seeks to create a closer connection between India’s handloom communities and contemporary audiences.

With its integrated approach to Handloom Excellence, Experience and Enterprise, Handloom Haat at Janpath is envisioned as a prominent destination where visitors can encounter the many dimensions of India’s handloom traditions- from the people and processes behind the cloth to its contemporary possibilities.

The inauguration on 14 August 2026 will mark the beginning of this new chapter for Handloom Haat, envisioned as “The Handloom Experience Centre”, a space where India’s living textile heritage can be seen, understood, experienced and taken forward.

headline: Vice President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Meets Parliamentary Delegation from Kenya

Wetang’ula, EGH, MP, Speaker of the National Assembly of Kenya, who is leading a Parliamentary Delegation from Kenya on a bilateral visit to India.

During the meeting, the Vice-President highlighted the close parliamentary ties between India and Kenya and expressed India’s readiness to share its experience in technology solutions and digital technology, including the use of digital technology leading towards a paperless Parliament. He noted the presence of an Indian-origin Member of Parliament in Kenya’s Parliamentary Friendship Group and recalled with appreciation the proposal to install a bust of Mahatma Gandhi within the premises of the National Assembly of Kenya.

The Vice-President recalled that Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had visited Kenya in 2016, followed by the visit of Hon’ble President Ruto to India in 2023.

Referring to India’s development partnership with Kenya, the Vice-President noted that several projects had been executed in the form of grant-in-aid, including the refurbishment of the Mahatma Gandhi Graduate Library of the University of Nairobi and the CT scan infrastructure at the Kenyan Navy Base, Mtongwe. He also recalled India’s assistance during the Ebola Virus Outbreak, when India delivered the first tranche of 4.5 tonnes of medical supplies.

The Vice-President highlighted India’s continued support for capacity building in Kenya. He stated that the Government of India offers around 400 scholarships, including training courses for various Government Ministries. He further noted that 20 diplomats from Kenya are undergoing capacity development in India. He informed that ICCR scholarships for long-term courses have been increased from 80 to 100 annually.

The Vice-President also highlighted the Agreement on the Digi-Locker pilot project in Kenya, which was signed during the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi. He further noted that Indian and Kenyan teams are working on the GATI Shakti project for Kenya.

The Vice-President thanked Kenya for supporting India’s candidature for the non-permanent seat in the United Nations Security Council for the term 2028–29. He sought Kenya’s support for India’s permanent membership in the United Nations Security Council.

Emphasising the historical ties between the two countries, the Vice-President noted that India and the Swahili coast had well-established trading routes for benefit of each other. He also expressed India’s hope that Kenya would join the International Solar Alliance and the International Big Cat Alliance.

The Vice President also highlighted the centuries-old people-to-people ties between India and Kenya and said that he was delighted to note that the Indian diaspora had been recognised as the 44th tribe of Kenya.

Concluding the meeting, the Vice President thanked the Kenyan Parliamentary Delegation for visiting India and conveyed his best wishes for a pleasant and productive stay. He expressed confidence that the visit would further deepen parliamentary engagement and contribute to strengthening the comprehensive partnership between India and Kenya.

headline: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of reported death of 19 CRPF personnel between January to May 2026, as per the official data compiled by CRPF
fullText:
National Human Rights Commission

NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of reported death of 19 CRPF personnel between January to May 2026, as per the official data compiled by CRPF

Reportedly, the CRPF recorded the highest 59 suicides by its personnel in 2025

The Commission issues notices to the Home Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs and the CRPF Director General, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks

14 AUG 2026 12:45PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that 19 Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel died by suicide in less than five months between January and 22nd May 2026. According to the reported CRPF data, the force lost 59 personnel due to suicide in 2025. Reportedly, this was the highest number of suicides recorded in the last five years.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of the right to life of the personnel working with the largest Central Armed Police Force of the country. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Home Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs and the CRPF Director General, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.

According to the media report, carried on 11th August 2026, a total of 281 CRPF personnel died by suicide in the last five years. Of these, approximately 216 were on duty. The CRPF recorded 57 suicides in 2021, 43 in 2022, 57 in 2023, 46 in 2024 and 59 in 2025.

headline: Creating a new milestone in the policy of zero tolerance against narcotics, NCB secures the return of fugitive drug kingpin Virender Singh Basoya from the UAE
fullText:
Ministry of Home Affairs

Creating a new milestone in the policy of zero tolerance against narcotics, NCB secures the return of fugitive drug kingpin Virender Singh Basoya from the UAE

Sharing details of Basoya's arrest, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah says - Modi government is relentlessly tracking down drug traffickers hiding abroad

The Modi government is destroying entire drug traffickers’ entire ecosystem with a ruthless approach

Wanted international drug trafficker Virender Singh Basoya brought back to India under 'Operation GLOBAL-HUNT'

By tracing the criminal through a top-to-bottom and bottom-to-top approach, our agencies have once again proven that no matter where drug traffickers hide, they cannot escape the long arm of Indian law

14 AUG 2026 12:31PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant success in the fight against transnational narcotics syndicates, the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has secured the return to India of wanted fugitive Virender Singh Basoya @ Viru @ Basoya, a resident of Pillanji, Sarojini Nagar, Delhi. He was taken into custody upon his arrival at IGI Airport, New Delhi, early this morning.

Basoya had been arrested in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in June 2026 pursuant to an INTERPOL Red Notice published at the request of NCB. His return to India was secured through sustained coordination with the UAE authorities by Indian agencies.

In a post on X platform, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said “Modi govt is relentlessly tracking down drug traffickers hiding abroad and destroying their entire ecosystem with a ruthless approach. Creating a new milestone in the policy of zero tolerance against narcotics, the NCB secured the return of fugitive drug kingpin Virender Singh Basoya from the UAE. By tracing the criminal through a top-to-bottom and bottom-to-top approach, our agencies have once again proven that no matter where drug traffickers hide, they cannot escape the long arm of Indian law.”

Modi govt is relentlessly tracking down drug traffickers hiding abroad and destroying their entire ecosystem with a ruthless approach.

Creating a new milestone in the policy of zero tolerance against narcotics, the NCB secured the return of fugitive drug kingpin Virender Singh…

— Amit Shah (@AmitShah) August 14, 2026

The case originated in Pune in February 2024, when Pune City Police seized 500 grams of Mephedrone. Thereafter, adopting a top-to-bottom and bottom-to-top approach, the investigation was expanded to identify and dismantle the entire drug trafficking network. Subsequent investigation and follow-up operations resulted in the recovery of approximately 867 kg of Mephedrone from Pune and 970 kg from Delhi, taking the total recovery to approximately 1,837 kg of Mephedrone. The case was subsequently transferred to the Mumbai Zonal Unit of NCB for further investigation.

Investigation identified Basoya as a key overseas operative and alleged conspirator who coordinated activities of the syndicate from abroad and facilitated the export of Mephedrone consignments from India to other countries. A major consignment of approximately 970 kg of Mephedrone, recovered in Delhi, was allegedly linked to preparations for export through courier channels associated with him. His role emerged as an important link connecting the domestic manufacturing and trafficking network with its overseas distribution channels.

Basoya also figures in a separate Delhi Police Special Cell case relating to international cocaine trafficking. In October 2024, the Special Cell of Delhi Police busted a major drug trafficking cartel, leading to multiple seizures from godowns and other premises in Delhi, Hapur and Ghaziabad, as well as from a factory in Ankleshwar, Gujarat. The coordinated operations resulted in the recovery of more than 1,300 kg of cocaine, Mephedrone and hydroponic weed. Investigation into the cartel revealed Basoya’s alleged role in coordinating the procurement, transportation, storage and distribution of cocaine and other drugs.

The return of Basoya is part of NCB’s sustained efforts under Operation GLOBAL-HUNT, launched to identify, locate and pursue major narcotics traffickers and fugitives operating from overseas jurisdictions. The initiative leverages international cooperation mechanisms, including INTERPOL Red Notices, and strengthens operational coordination with Indian and foreign law-enforcement agencies. The earlier successful return of other wanted drug traffickers, including Mohammad Salim Dola from Türkiye and Navin Chichkar from Malaysia, were also significant achievements under this initiative.

Bringing back fugitives to India to face legal consequences of their crimes is in furtherance of the Vision Document on Drug Control (2026–2029), unveiled by the Hon’ble Union Home Minister As part of this roadmap, sustained efforts are underway to identify, locate and bring back other important narcotics fugitives operating from abroad through coordinated action with other national and international agencies.

Under the leadership of the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the guidance of the Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah, NCB remains firmly committed to the Government of India’s policy of Zero Tolerance against Drug Trafficking.

NCB will continue to pursue drug kingpins, financiers, handlers and fugitives, whether operating from within India or abroad, and work closely with national and international partners to dismantle the entire narcotics trafficking ecosystem.

headline: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported death of one person and injuries to another after inhaling toxic gases while cleaning a manhole at a factory in Faridabad district, Haryana
fullText:
National Human Rights Commission

NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported death of one person and injuries to another after inhaling toxic gases while cleaning a manhole at a factory in Faridabad district, Haryana

Issues a notice to the Haryana Chief Secretary and Faridabad Police Commissioner, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks

The report expected to include the status of the investigation of the case, health of the injured as well as compensation, if any, provided to him and the NoK of the deceased

14 AUG 2026 12:30PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that on 11th August 2026, one person died and another got injured after inhaling toxic gases while cleaning a manhole at a factory in Sector-25 of Faridabad district, Haryana. Reportedly, they descended into the manhole without any safety equipment.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Haryana Chief Secretary and Faridabad Police Commissioner, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. The report is expected to include the status of the investigation, health of the injured, as well as compensation, if any, provided to him and the NoK of the deceased.

According to the media report, carried on 11th August 2026, the workers were called by the factory owner to clean the manhole.

headline: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported snake bite of six girls leading to three deaths in a hostel in Gadchiroli district, Maharashtra
fullText:
National Human Rights Commission

NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported snake bite of six girls leading to three deaths in a hostel in Gadchiroli district, Maharashtra

Reportedly, students slept on the floor due to lack of cots

The Commission issues a notice to the Maharashtra Chief Secretary, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks

The report expected to include the health status of the injured

14 AUG 2026 12:28PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that six girl students, belonging to the Scheduled Tribe, were bitten by a snake in a hostel of an Ashram school in Gadchiroli district, Maharashtra. Reportedly, they were sleeping on the floor inside their hostel room due to lack of cots. Three of the victim students succumbed to the snake bite, while the remaining three were undergoing treatment at a hospital.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Maharashtra Chief Secretary, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. The report is expected to include the health status of the injured girl students.

According to the media report, carried on 11th August 2026, 79 girl students are accommodated in a single room of the hostel. The hostel, which has been functional for the last 25 years, lacks basic facilities. Every year, the district reports a significant number of snake bite cases.

(Release ID: 2299316)

Measures taken by the Software technology Parks of India (STPI) to streamline approvals and improve ease of doing business for STP units are as follows:

Automation of Statutory Services: For providing seamless services to the IT exporters, statutory services including SOFTEX filling, its approval and final intimation to them has been automated. This has ensured speedy delivery of services to the satisfaction of the IT industry.

Integration with RBI’s Export Data Processing and Monitoring System (EDPMS) System for IT exporters: STPI’s online system for IT exporters has been integrated with the Reserve Bank of India’s EDPMS for sharing of export data. This integration has enabled seamless electronic transmission of export declaration data to RBI in near real time. This has facilitated faster exchange of export data, enhanced accuracy and transparency, reduced manual intervention, improved monitoring of export transactions, and streamlined regulatory compliance for IT/ITeS exporters.

Simplification of Import Procedures: The earlier practice of case-to-case import permissions has been replaced with blanket import permissions for the financial year concerned.

Self-Declaration for Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) Sales: The requirement for prior DTA permissions for STPI-registered units has been replaced with a submission of self-declaration (except for advance DTA sales in first year of operation).

headline: FutureSkills PRIME Strengthens India’s Future Ready Digital Workforce Through Skilling in Emerging Technologies
fullText:
Ministry of Electronics & IT

FutureSkills PRIME Strengthens India’s Future Ready Digital Workforce Through Skilling in Emerging Technologies

Over 34 Lakh Candidates Registered on FutureSkills PRIME Portal; 13 Lakh+ Candidates Certified

14 AUG 2026 11:46AM by PIB Delhi

Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister, the Government of India is preparing a future-ready workforce. These skills are required in an ecosystem of cutting-edge technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data Analytics, Cyber Security, Internet of Things (IoT), Semiconductors, Cloud Computing, etc across key sectors.

India is a skills capital in IT and known for its strong talent pipeline and skilled workforce, with its IT sector globally recognised for high-quality talent. As per global assessments such as the Stanford AI Index, India ranks among the leading nations in AI adoption, preparedness and ecosystem vibrancy. India also accounts for around 20% of the global semiconductor design workforce, reflecting its emphasis on skilling and talent development. With the rapid adoption of digital technologies across sectors, developing a digitally skilled workforce has become critical for sustaining this growth.

The Government accords priority to digital skilling and capacity building of youth across the country, including those from North Eastern and Himalayan region. Towards this objective, various Ministries and Departments in partnership with industry and with active contribution from academia and R&D institutions are implementing flagship programmes to promote digital literacy, employability and skills in emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Cyber Security, Data Analytics, Drone Technology, Cloud Computing and Semiconductor Design.

Digital India Programme:

As part of the same strategy, the Government of India launched the Digital India Programme in July, 2015 and has been taking steps to ensure that we continue to retain our advantage in IT skills and is promoting skilling in emerging technologies through various initiatives including FutureSkills PRIME programme, so that digital technologies improve the life of every citizen, expand India’s digital economy and create investment and employment opportunities in India. These programmes have enabled large-scale participation of youth and professionals across the country. The outreach model is not only implemented through the FutureSkills PRIME portal but is also supported by the resource centres of C-DAC and NIELIT.

FutureSkills PRIME Programme:

Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology has initiated a programme titled “FutureSkills PRIME” (FSP), jointly with NASSCOM (National Association of Software and Services Companies.) for skilling/ re-skilling/ up-skilling of candidates in new/emerging technologies, aimed at making India a cutting-edge digital talent nation. The FutureSkills PRIME offers industry aligned courses. The platform is an agile model that allows continuous updation of skilling courses in sync with the skill demand.

Key features are:

● Skilling, reskilling, and upskilling in emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Big Data Analytics, IoTs, Cyber Security, Blockchain, AR/VR, etc.

● Courses are developed in the consultation with industry to align with actual employment needs.

● The Portal can be accessible online anytime-anywhere to earn skill certificates in line with their aptitude and aspirations at https://futureskillsprime.in/

● Currently, the FSP portal hosts more than 500 courses which are industry aligned and various Global OEM partners are collaborating as part of the FSP ecosystem.

● So far, more than 34 lakh candidates have registered on the portal, out of which there have been 23 lakh+ candidates enrolled/trained in various courses, out of which 13 lakh+ candidates have been completed/certified. This includes 41% women and over 86% candidates are from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

● In addition, 22 CDAC/NIELIT Centres have been grouped as Lead and Co-Lead Resource Centres (RCs) for the 10 emerging technologies, and they are mandated to train the Government officials and conduct the bootcamps.

● In total, the Resource Centres (RCs) have trained 32,700+ Government officials, 2,367 trainers and 40,400+ candidates under more than 420+ bootcamps.

The primary objective of these Data and AI Labs is capacity building and skill development. Accordingly, the Labs are focusing on training and certification activities.

fullText:

PM Vishwakarma Beneficiaries Invited as ‘Special Guests’ to Witness 80th Independence Day Ceremony at Red Fort, Delhi

100 beneficiaries from Delhi-NCR to attend the Celebration

14 AUG 2026 10:45AM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has invited 100 beneficiaries of PM Vishwakarma from the Delhi-NCR region as ‘Special Guests’ to witness the 80th Independence Day Ceremony at the Red Fort, Delhi, on 15th August, 2026. The beneficiaries will attend the national celebration along with their spouse/companion.

The Special Guests also include women artisans from various traditional trades, reflecting the scheme’s contribution towards women’s economic empowerment, greater participation in livelihoods and strengthening the role of women in preserving India’s rich artisanal and cultural heritage.

Recognition and Appreciation of Beneficiaries-

As part of their participation, the PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries will also be presented with souvenirs as a token of recognition and appreciation, followed by an interaction with officials of the Ministry of MSME on 14 August 2026 at the Indian Institute of Public Administration, Delhi, recognising their contribution to India’s traditional crafts and cultural heritage.

About PM Vishwakarma Scheme-

PM Vishwakarma is one of the flagship initiatives of the Government of India aimed at providing comprehensive support to artisans and craftspeople engaged in traditional trades. The scheme provides assistance through skill upgradation, modern tools, financial support, digital enablement and market linkages, with the objective of promoting the socio-economic empowerment of artisans, strengthening traditional crafts and ensuring sustainable livelihoods. Under the scheme, 30 lakh traditional artisans and craftspeople have been registered.

Celebrating the Contribution of India’s Traditional Artisans & Craftspeople

The invited beneficiaries represent the 18 traditional trades covered under PM Vishwakarma, including Tailor, Carpenter, Goldsmith, Blacksmith, Locksmith, among others. The beneficiaries invited have availed various benefits under the scheme, including registration, Basic Skill Training and provision of toolkits, along with other support benefits available under the scheme.

The participation of PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries in the Independence Day celebration is recognition of the invaluable contribution of traditional artisans and craftspeople to India’s rich cultural heritage. fullText:
Ministry of Railways

Railway Minister Reviews Progress of Passenger Holding Areas at Anand Vihar and Udhna Stations

Yatri Suvidha Kendras to Manage Festival Rush and Provide Safer, More Organised Passenger Movement

14 AUG 2026 6:11PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw today reviewed the progress of passenger holding area projects at Anand Vihar Terminal and Udhna Railway Station from Rail Bhawan, New Delhi. Union Minister of State for Railways, Shri V. Somanna was also present in the meeting. The review focused on expediting ongoing works, addressing site-related challenges and ensuring timely completion of the facilities. It also covered civil works, removal of obstructions, utility shifting, structural works, passenger amenities and other associated facilities. The Yatri Suvidha Kendra is to be completed before the forthcoming major festival rush to provide safer, more organised and passenger-centric arrangements.

The Yatri Suvidha Kendras (Passenger Holding Areas) are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers, helping decongest station platforms, circulating areas and station approaches during peak passenger movement. The facilities are designed to ensure orderly passenger circulation and provide a comfortable waiting environment before passengers enter the station/platform area.

The Kendras will provide spacious covered waiting and seating areas, dedicated ticketing facilities, toilets and washroom facilities for men and women, drinking water and other essential passenger amenities. Public Address and passenger information systems, CCTV surveillance and security arrangements, adequate lighting, electrical and S&T facilities, display boards, signage, organised passenger circulation and furniture are also being provided.

Anand Vihar Terminal

At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra is being developed in two phases. Phase-I will provide organised space for approximately 4,000 passengers, with work on foundations, plinth beams, structural steel fabrication and other associated activities progressing at a fast pace.

Phase-II will further strengthen the facility’s passenger-handling capacity, enabling it to accommodate around 7,000 passengers on completion.

Udhna Railway Station

At Udhna Railway Station, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra is planned to accommodate around 15,000 passengers at a time. Significant progress has already been achieved at site.

After completion, the Udhna station will provide improved connectivity between the holding area and the platforms, supporting the orderly movement of passengers and better management of passenger flows within the station premises.

The Yatri Suvidha Kendras at Anand Vihar Terminal and Udhna Railway Station will strengthen Indian Railways’ capacity to handle large passenger gatherings in a safe, comfortable and organised manner, while reducing congestion and improving passenger movement during peak travel periods.

The initiatives reflect Indian Railways’ continued focus on upgrading passenger infrastructure at major stations through improved facilities, technology and organised passenger management, ensuring a more seamless travel experience for the millions of passengers who rely on the railway network every day.

headline: Partition was one of the largest mass migrations in human history, says Vice-President on the occasion of Partition Horrors Remembrance Day
fullText:
Vice President's Secretariat

Partition was one of the largest mass migrations in human history, says Vice-President on the occasion of Partition Horrors Remembrance Day

Freedom is precious, unity is essential, peace can never be taken for granted: Vice-President

Partition was more than redrawing of borders; it divided a civilisational heritage built over thousands of years: VP

Our children deserve to know the truth of Partition: Vice-President

Hurried redrawing of borders created disputes that continue to have implications even today: Vice President

No caste, language or region is more important than the nation: Vice-President

14 AUG 2026 6:08PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed a National Seminar on the occasion of Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, organised by the Centre for Independence and Partition Studies, University of Delhi, in association with the Indian Council of Historical Research (ICHR). The seminar was held on the theme ‘The Partition of India - A Saga of Displacement, Separation and Resettlement’ and focused on The Story of India’s Partition (1947).

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed a National Seminar on the occasion of Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, organised by the Centre for Independence and Partition Studies, University of Delhi, in association with the Indian Council of Historical Research… pic.twitter.com/jL9imDfFpA

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) August 14, 2026

Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President paid his deep respects to the survivors of Partition who were present at the seminar and said that the nation had gathered to reflect on “one of the most tragic and dehumanising chapters” in its history.

The Vice-President emphasised that the purpose of remembering Partition is not to reopen old wounds with bitterness, but to move towards greater unity and harmony. As Bharat prepares to celebrate Independence Day, he said, the nation must pause to remember the sacrifices and suffering of those who lived through Partition.

Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan noted that Independence brought freedom from colonial rule, but was accompanied by an unprecedented tragedy and one of the largest mass migrations in human history. He said that the scale of the tragedy remains a stark warning of the devastating consequences of division and hatred.

The Vice-President appreciated the University of Delhi for establishing the Centre for Independence and Partition Studies in 2023, dedicated to preserving and studying this history. He noted that, in a short period, the Centre has recorded the oral testimonies of more than a hundred Partition survivors and continues to engage young students through lectures, archives and public events.

“Our children deserve to know the truth of Partition,” Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said, stressing that a catastrophe of such magnitude cannot be reduced to a few lines in a textbook. He recalled the enduring wisdom that those who fail to remember the past risk repeating its tragedies.

Referring to the wider historical consequences of Partition, the Vice-President said that the hurried redrawing of borders created disputes that continue to have implications even today. He noted that Partition has had a lasting impact on India’s defence policy, national security and relations with neighbouring countries.

Reflecting on the lessons of Partition and the importance of leadership in times of crisis, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that the will and determination of political leadership are important in taking difficult decisions in the larger national interest.

Recalling the incidents during Partition, the Vice-President emphasised the importance of preparedness and responsible decision-making, noting that decisions having a bearing on the safety and security of people should be taken with adequate advance notice. He stressed that the safety and security of everyone must always remain a paramount consideration.

He further observed that Partition was not merely a redrawing of political boundaries, but also divided a civilisational landscape that had remained interconnected for thousands of years. He referred to the disruption of access to several important civilisational, cultural and spiritual sites, including the Sindhu river, Kartarpur Sahib, Nankana Sahib, ancient Shaktipeeths, and the archaeological heritage of Harappa, Mohenjodaro and Takshashila.

The Vice-President urged citizens to place the nation above narrower identities and emphasised that no caste, language or region can be more important than the nation. He said that every Indian should feel proud of being Indian and remain conscious of the shared civilisational heritage and national identity that binds the country together.

During the occasion, the Vice-President felicitated 15 Partition survivors in recognition of their courage, resilience and contribution to preserving the memories and lived experiences of Partition.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan felicitated the Partition survivors in recognition of their courage, resilience and contribution to preserving the memories and lived experiences of Partition on the occasion of Partition Horrors Remembrance Day in University of Delhi… pic.twitter.com/N4e24iTsio

The Vice-President also administered the ‘No Drugs’ pledge to the students, urging the younger generation to stay away from drugs and make healthy, responsible and constructive choices for their future.

Concluding his address, the Vice-President said that Partition Horrors Remembrance Day should remind the nation that freedom is precious, unity is essential and peace can never be taken for granted.

The Vice-President also witnessed an exhibition organised by the ICHR and the University of Delhi on the occasion. He said that the exhibits offered a powerful reminder of the enormous human cost of Partition.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan also witnessed an exhibition organised by the ICHR and the University of Delhi on the occasion of Partition Horrors Remembrance Day. He said that the exhibits offered a powerful reminder of the enormous human cost of Partition. pic.twitter.com/wBF2Wgm0r5

The seminar was attended by Vice-Chancellor, University of Delhi, Prof. Yogesh Singh; Chairman, ICHR, Prof. Raghuvendra Tanwar; Dean of Colleges, Prof. Balram Pani; Registrar, Dr. Vikas Gupta, besides academics, scholars, students and Partition survivors.

headline: Military modernisation driven by a self-reliant & future-ready defence sector is Govt’s top priority: Raksha Mantri on the eve of 80th Independence Day
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

Military modernisation driven by a self-reliant & future-ready defence sector is Govt’s top priority: Raksha Mantri on the eve of 80th Independence Day

14 AUG 2026 5:38PM by PIB Delhi

“The Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, is according the highest priority to the modernisation of the defence forces driven by a self-reliant and future-ready defence sector,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh in his address to the soldiers through Akashvani on the eve of 80th Independence Day on August 14, 2026. Highlighting the transformative shift witnessed by the defence sector in the last 12 years due to the initiatives such as ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ and ‘Make-in-India’, Raksha Mantri asserted that India has become a nation which is effectively catering to its own security needs, while emerging as a global defence manufacturing hub and a net defence exporter.

Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised that the domestic defence production, which stood at just Rs 46,000 crore in 2014, has skyrocketed to a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in the Financial Year (FY) 2025-26, nearly a four-fold increase over the last decade. This achievement, he said, is a testament to the structural changes that have taken place in the defence sector. He pointed out that Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) and other public sector entities accounted for approximately 76% of the total defence production, with the private sector contributing 24%, up from 22% in the previous fiscal year. This growing participation of the private sector signals a continuously improving business environment within the defence sector, he said.

Raksha Mantri added that defence exports, which stood at a mere Rs 686 crore in FY 2013-14, surged to an all-time high of Rs 38,424 crore in FY 2025-26, an increase of over 5,500%. He described the feat as the most compelling evidence of Aatmanirbharta in the defence sector. “Today, India has 145 defence exporters, and our products are being exported to over 80 countries. I am confident that we will achieve our defence exports target of Rs 50,000 crore by 2029,” he said.

Shri Rajnath Singh also pointed out that the defence budget has risen from Rs 2.53 lakh crore in FY 2013-14 to Rs 7.85 lakh crore in FY 2026-27, which is a reflection of India's growing commitment to future defence technologies. “Capital expenditure has grown from Rs 94,588 crore to Rs 2.19 lakh crore. Our focus on Research & Development has also intensified. The R&D budget, which stood at Rs 15,283 crore in FY 2014-15, has increased by 90% to Rs 29,100 crore in FY 2026-27,” he said.

Raksha Mantri added that over the past year, the Defence Acquisition Council has granted Acceptance of Necessity for projects worth over Rs 8.75 lakh crore, which highlights the Government’s emphasis on defence modernisation. He listed the fundamental reforms undertaken in defence procurement to accelerate this modernisation process, including a two-fold increase in financial ceiling for Field Commanders to strengthen operational efficiency, and facilitation of procurement worth more than Rs 1.25 lakh crore through the revenue route to boost indigenisation.

Shri Rajnath Singh acknowledged the enthusiastic participation of the defence forces in the journey towards Aatmanirbharta. He stressed that India’s defence self-reliance drive is gaining momentum as indigenous warships, aircraft and advanced military systems are strengthening the capabilities of the Defence Forces.

Raksha Mantri asserted that DRDO and the defence forces are positioning India at the forefront of technologies for future warfare amidst the evolving defence landscape. He made special mention of the successful test of the first Tactical Advanced Range Augmentation system, which has the capability to transform conventional weapons into precision-guided munitions. “The testing of the Advanced Agni Missile, equipped with MIRV technology, has added a new dimension to the strategic deterrence capabilities. Successful trials of the Long-Range Land Attack Cruise Missile, RudraM-II Air-to-Surface Missile, Naval Anti-Ship Missile-SR, and Pinaka Long-Range Guided Rocket have provided unprecedented strength to the nation’s strike capabilities,” he added.

On the successful test of Active Cooled Full-Scale Scramjet Combustor for over 1,200 seconds, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the feat has placed India among the select group of nations capable of developing hypersonic missile technology. He added that the nation’s air defence capabilities have been further bolstered by the first successful test of the indigenous Kusha’ Long-Range Surface-to-Air Missile.

Raksha Mantri underlined that border area development is a focus area of the Government as the objective is to enhance defence preparedness and connectivity with border areas. He lauded the defence forces for being the ‘first responders’ to carry out relief and rescue operations whenever an unfortunate natural disaster occurs in the country or abroad.

Shri Rajnath Singh reiterated the Government’s commitment towards the welfare of serving and retired defence forces personnel as well as their families, describing them as a reflection of honor, dignity, and self-respect. “Over the past five years, there has been a 300% increase in the budget of the Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme. Furthermore, under the Armed Forces Flag Day Fund, the Penury Grant has been doubled from Rs 4,000 to Rs 8,000, the Education Grant from Rs 1,000 to Rs 2,000 and the Marriage Grant from Rs 50,000 to Rs 1,00,000. These decisions demonstrate our commitment to the welfare of our soldiers and their Next-of-Kin,” he said.

Raksha Mantri also underscored the Government’s continued focus on providing increased opportunities for women in the defence forces and effectively utilising Nari Shakti in national security & nation building. “We achieved a historic milestone when the first batch of female cadets trained at the National Defence Academy was commissioned as officers in the three Services. This is proof that courage and leadership are not confined to any gender. ‘Samudra Pradakshina’, the first tri-service all-women circumnavigation sailing expedition onboard Indian Army Sailing Vessel Triveni, stands as a symbol of ‘New India’ powered by ‘Nari Shakti’, he said.

Their courage, commitment and discipline serve as a source of inspiration to every Indian. The nation will remain forever indebted to their unparalleled service, sacrifice, and dedication,” he said, expressing gratitude to every soldier.

Raksha Mantri stressed that the Independence Day this year holds special significance as 2026 marks the 150th anniversary of the National Song ‘Vande Mataram’. “It is our collective responsibility to celebrate the occasion with great enthusiasm. It is not merely an anniversary, but a celebration of our collective consciousness. I am confident that this Independence Day will continue to fuel the spirit of patriotism and service to the nation within every citizen. Let us pledge to become active participants in nation-building and, by discharging our duties with dedication, make meaningful contributions towards building Viksit Bharat,” he said while concluding his address.
